info.title: X Calls API
info.description: Start, join and schedule X calls as your app's user, and put a voice agent in them. In development: endpoints and payloads may change.

post.description: Starts an X call hosted by the authenticated user (typically a bot). Pass an XChat conversation_id to start the call in that conversation, or omit it for a standalone call anyone can join with the returned join_url (subject to join_policy). The call starts empty: put an agent in it with POST /2/calls/:id/join. When the host joins a conversation call, the other members are rung.

get.description:
Returns the X calls on the authenticated user's calendar, earliest first: events on their X Calls calendar, and events on the Google or Outlook calendars they linked to X whose conference is an X call. Calls still running at start_time are included. The window defaults to the next 24 hours and may span at most 7 days.

When both are provided, `start_time` must be earlier than `end_time`.

parameters.description: Calls still running at this time or starting after it (RFC 3339). Defaults to now.
parameters.name: start_time

parameters.description: Calls starting before this time (RFC 3339). Defaults to 24 hours after start_time.
parameters.name: end_time

parameters.description: The most calls to return. Defaults to 20.
parameters.name: max_results

post.description: Puts an X call on the authenticated user's X Calls calendar, with them as its organizer, and invites people to it. The call exists right away: share its join_url, or put an agent in it at start time with POST /2/calls/:id/join. A recurrence (an RFC 5545 RRULE) repeats it. Invitees get an email unless notify_invitees is false.

delete.description: Cancels a scheduled call the authenticated user organizes, and takes it off invitees' calendars. For a recurring call, scope and occurrence_start_time pick the occurrences: all of them (the default), one, or one and every one after it. Cancelling what is already cancelled succeeds.

parameters.description: Which occurrences: all (the default without occurrence_start_time), this (the default with it), or this_and_following.
parameters.name: scope

parameters.description: Start of the occurrence that scope this or this_and_following refers to (RFC 3339).
parameters.name: occurrence_start_time

parameters.description: Whether invitees get an email about it. Defaults to true.
parameters.name: notify_invitees

get.description: Returns a scheduled call the authenticated user organizes or is invited to, at its occurrence running now or its next one within a year: its time, call, recurrence and who is invited and how they answered. Changes can take a few seconds to show here.

put.description: Moves, renames or re-invites a scheduled call the authenticated user organizes. Only the fields sent change. For a recurring call, scope and occurrence_start_time pick the occurrences: all of them (the default), one, or one and every one after it.

post.description: Accepts, declines or tentatively accepts an invitation to a scheduled call for the authenticated user. For a recurring call, scope and occurrence_start_time pick the occurrences the answer is for: all of them (the default), one, or one and every one after it.

get.description: Returns a call's title, join policy, host and participant count, and whether the authenticated user may join it without asking the host.

post.description: Starts a media session that takes part in the call as the authenticated user. The response carries a media_url and a short-lived media_token: open a WebSocket to media_url with the token as a Bearer credential to exchange PCM16 audio and events with the call; the user enters the call when the WebSocket connects. On a closed or trusted call the session asks the host first (admission: requires_approval).
Ends the authenticated user's media session in the call (its WebSocket receives session.ended with reason left) and removes the user from the call.
